note: Camp life at Willow Bend: barks (one line when Ruth walks up) and fireside conversations (two to four lines), picked by src/ai/camp.gd from story flags, Standing, money, bounties, recent crimes (WorldState.crimes_log), kills, catches and the chapter. Conditions: flag {name: value}, flag_set [names], chapter_min/max, standing_min/max, money_min/max, bounty_min, kills_civilian_min, kills_outlaw_min, recent_crime kind, item_prefix. Original writing.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Stew's on. Mostly beans, some rabbit, and a carrot that wandered in on its own.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Folk in Bitter Spring tip their hats to you now. Took me ten years to get a nod, and that was from a mule.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Man at the store asked if I ride with you. I said I cook for you. Seemed safer, the way he asked.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Your face is up by the depot again. They've made you uglier this time. I took it personal, on behalf of the camp.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: That's good meat you're carrying. Give it here before it turns, and I'll make something a Christian could eat.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Cold makes stew taste better. My mother said so, and we were very cold, so she'd know.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Red seven on the black eight. The cards behave when nobody's betting. So do I, mostly.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: You're carrying more than a hundred dollars, cher. I can smell it from here. Don't leave it near me after midnight.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Five dollars to your name. I've seen bigger fortunes in a church plate, and that was a Methodist church.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Old Merrow sends his regards from Port Linden. He's taken up religion. Something moderate, he says.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: I heard about the hold-up. Sloppy, cher. You stood where the witness could see your scar.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Marcus Aurelius. He says the obstacle is the way. He never rode a mule through the Breaks.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: One. It's always one. The trick is how many times one comes round before supper.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Rosa Ybarra writes that Inés runs faster than her brothers. I've kept the letter. Tell no one.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Inés walks with a hitch. Her mother says the girl's proud of it. I'm not.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: You've killed people who weren't shooting at you. I've sewn up enough of the other kind to know the difference.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Your mare was favouring her off hind. It was a stone. I got it out. You can thank me with coffee.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Is it true they'd pay two hundred dollars for you? I'd never turn you in. I'm only asking what I'm worth by association.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I rode swing on a real drive. Did I tell you? I'll tell you again later in case you forget.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: You got a pelt! Can I scrape it? I know how. Mostly. Hap showed me once.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Del says you've killed more men than the cholera. Is that meant nice?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The Lantern says the syndicate is a benevolent enterprise. Page four, under the notices for strayed cattle.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: This cinch is half rot. Whoever sold it to you should be ashamed of himself, or at least richer.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I think about the boy going west. I hope he made it. I hope he never comes back.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Snow's off the ridge now. I keep thinking it should have covered more than it did.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: People are starting to say your name the way they say Shale's. I'd stop giving them reasons.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Boy, you sit on that side, where the smoke isn't. Mrs. Caddell, you sit wherever you like. You've earned it twice today.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Are we staying? Here? For good?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: For tonight. Good's a long word.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Miss Arceneaux. Do you play cards with the Lord's money?

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Only on Sundays, Mr. Lindqvist. The rest of the week it's mine.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: She's teaching Billy to count.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: That's what worries me.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Have you seen your price lately? I'm jealous. Nobody ever offered two hundred for me. Not even honestly.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: It's not a compliment, Miss Del.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's an invoice. Pell's sending it to whoever wants to collect.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Billy says you held up a man on the road.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Billy talks.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Billy worships you. That's worse. He'll do what you do, only sooner, and with less sense.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: There's blood on your cuff that isn't yours, and nobody was shooting at you. So I'm told.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You're told a lot, Doctor.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I'm a doctor. People confess to me. Even the ones who never come near the tent.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: They're saying in Bitter Spring a man was killed who never drew. They're saying it was you.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And what are you saying?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: I'm saying the stew's hot. I'm not saying anything else until you tell me it wasn't.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: A woman in Bitter Spring asked me to thank you. Didn't say for what. Only thank you.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: That's the best kind. The kind you can't spend.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I don't know her.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: She knows you. That's how it goes, now.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Preacher in Bitter Spring mentioned you in his sermon. Not by name. He said, a certain widow. Everybody turned round.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Was it a kind mention?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: He said you'd done more good with a revolver than he'd done with a hymnal. He looked sorry about it.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: We're becoming notorious, Doctor.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: We were notorious. Now we're famous for the wrong things, which is notorious with better posters.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Say it plain, the pair of you.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: People cross the street, Ruth. Even the ones who used to cross it toward us.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Cutter Shale in Mabry's jail. I keep saying it to myself like a man counting money.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Count it slowly. Pell will have him out the minute a judge needs a new roof.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then the judge will have to say so out loud, in a courtroom. That's something.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Doc, is it wrong to be glad somebody's dead?

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Glad is allowed, Billy. It's proud that rots you. Ask Ruth which one she is.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Neither. Tired. Go to bed, Billy.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: A drop for the doctor? It's a cold night and I'm feeling generous with Hap's whiskey.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Coffee, please. Forty days. I'm told it gets easier. I'm told a great many things by people who've never tried.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll get the pot.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: That's your third, Doc.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Second. The first one doesn't count. It was medicinal. So was the second, come to think.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Your hands were steady at the Ybarras'. Don't make me wish I'd said no.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Ruth brought a pelt back! Hap, can we sell it? Can we sell it and buy a saddle?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: We can sell it and buy flour, which is a saddle for the stomach.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Flour. Then we'll see about saddles.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Read me the part about us, Joseph.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: There isn't a part about us. There's a part about a widow and her desperadoes. You're a desperado.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I'm a desperado!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Joseph. Don't.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Joseph says you let the youngest Shale go. Sent him west.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He held the horses.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: My father held horses for a man who robbed a bank in Uppsala. Then he held horses for a doctor for forty years. People are what they hold next.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Joseph hasn't said ten words since the Kestrel. That's unusual even for him.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Nine. I've been counting.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Say the tenth, then.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Later.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Hap, did you ever ride swing?

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: I rode drag for eleven years, boy. Swing is for people with prospects.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I've got prospects! Ruth said I'm a hand.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Ruth, you're carrying enough to buy a riverboat. A small one. With a leak.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's for the camp.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Then put some in the ledger before I think of a better use for it. I always do.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: The flour sack's light, and so's your purse, if you'll forgive me looking.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's been a lean month.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Then we eat beans and call it a feast. I've had worse feasts with more money.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: You never say much about Tom.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He wound his watch every night and never once set it right. Said the time was what you made it.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Sounds like a man who'd have liked my stew.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He'd have lied and said so. He was kind like that.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: First snow on the Kestrel. The passes will close in a week.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Then whoever's on the other side stays there. Can't say I mind which side that is, tonight.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Eben's on our side of the mountain. He always is.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Fellow came by in a steam buggy asking for the shareholder. Set fire to a sage bush and left a pamphlet. I started the stew with it.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Clementine Voss sent a pie and a note. Says Lyman Gage works like a man trying to outrun something.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Mrs. Voss sent a pie. No note this time. Just the pie. That's a note too, in its way.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A phrenologist in Mesquite Wells tells the whole cantina you've the bump of commerce. I've examined your head myself. I found a scar.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Ramon Ortiz's boy came to me with a split lip from a mule. He says he's to be a farmer now. The bumps were wrong, he says.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I'm told you poured a saloon into the mud at Coldwater. Rye whiskey, eleven years old. I've wept at funerals with less cause.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A temperance woman and a saloonkeeper sharing coffee. If you can manage that, you can manage Pell. Possibly even me.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: A Chicago detective wrote to the Gilded Spur asking after your health. Drunk, by the handwriting. He says he owes you one.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Mabry let your detective out by supper, like he said he would. He's drinking at the Gilded Spur and toasting you, not kindly.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: The loggers at Thornwood poured out forty bottles of Marvel's Elixir. They say the creek's never been so calm.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Cassius Mulvey. I knew him in Natchez. He sold me a lucky bean. I've still got it, and that's the whole trouble with luck.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: A lady photographer in Thornwood says you smashed a plate worth forty thousand copies. Vanity, cher, or modesty? I can never tell with you.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Is it you on the cover? Miss Ruthie Rides Again! You've got two guns and the cougar's the size of a horse.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Hap says a man robbed you with your own canteen still in his hand. I'd have thought you'd see that coming. Don't hit me.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Fenn printed a map of a water line nobody admits to building. Pell's men tear the Lantern off the fences faster than the boys can paste it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: That railroad surveyor in the Breaks says you returned his book unread. I hope he's wrong about the unread part.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You came down off the Kestrel looking like you'd been to a burying.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: An old man showed me a comet and died before it set. He'd waited nineteen years for it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: My grandmother said the sky keeps an account. Nineteen years is a long time to be owed.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It paid him. That's more than most of us get.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: There's a boy in Port Linden telling everybody you paid his debts. Pip something. Says you're his guardian angel with a gun.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I owed him a ride and some sense. He's sweeping the Lantern's press room now.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I sweep here. Nobody calls me an angel.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You'd hate it. Angels can't ride.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Is it true you knocked down Mick Rourke and two of his boys in front of the Lantern?

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Mick Rourke is telling it the other way round, cher. Port Linden believes whoever's still standing at the bar.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then I'll stay away from the bar.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Is it true you own part of a horseless carriage? Hap says it blew up a henhouse.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Two henhouses. The second one was on purpose. Testing, he called it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Twenty dollars' worth of the future, Billy. Mind you never stand in front of it.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: A man went by on the Greer road in a buggy with no horse, smoking like a stove. He waved. He said you'd missed your chance.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've missed a good many chances. That one I missed on purpose.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Sit. Eat. Don't tell me what's in it and I won't tell you either.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: You've had your bowl. The rest is for the boy, who's growing, and me, who's past it.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Coffee, then. Black as a lawyer's heart and twice as bitter. Your health, such as it is.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: One for you, one for me. Here's to steady hands, and to the people who don't need them.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Five cards, a quarter ante, and no stacked decks. I'd know. Cut.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: You took me. I let you, of course. I'll stop letting you any time now.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Don't look so wounded, cher. It's only money. It's only your money.
